description: The plot shows how classification accuracy (ACC) varies with co-occurrence number for six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME). The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning roughly from about 5 on the left to about 3000 on the right, with major ticks shown at 0, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging from 60 to 85 with labeled ticks at 60, 65, 70, 75, and 80. The Base line is black with circular markers and a solid stroke, increasing from about 61 at the smallest co-occurrence value to about 67 at the largest, with intermediate points near 63.5 and 65. The FT line is blue with downward-triangle markers and a solid stroke, rising from about 62.5 to about 68.5, passing through roughly 65 and 67.8. The IKE line is red with upward-triangle markers and a solid stroke, increasing from about 64.5 to about 70.2, with midpoints around 67.8 and 69.4. The MEND line is brown with diamond markers and a solid stroke, moving from about 66.0 to about 74.0, with intermediate values near 71.3 and 73.5. The MEMIT line is purple with pentagon markers and a solid stroke, increasing from about 66.5 to about 72.7, with midpoints around 70.2 and 71.4. The ROME line is green with square markers and a solid stroke, rising from about 72.3 to about 77.7, with intermediate points near 76.0 and 77.6 and a near-flat change between the last two x-values.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) performance of six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) on Llama2 across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents 'Co-occurrence Number' on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, while the y-axis shows 'ACC (%)' on a linear scale from 60% to 80%. ROME consistently outperforms all other methods, achieving an accuracy of approximately 85% at the highest co-occurrence number. MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, with MEMIT slightly surpassing MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers but falling behind at higher values. FT demonstrates the steepest growth rate, increasing by nearly 10% across the range, while Base remains relatively stable, showing minimal improvement. IKE starts with the highest initial accuracy but stabilizes at around 70%, falling behind MEMIT and MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers.
